COMMENTS

These WebSphere Application Server messages are written to the SystemOut.log file for the Process Center in situations where the Process Designer web editor has been running for a long period of time. They do not affect any functionality and can be safely ignored.

Tivoli Integrated Portal uses LTPA (IBM Lightweight Third-Party Authentication) as default authentication mechanism for WebSphere Application Server.
The LTPA time out is configured in the security.xml file in TIP, and by default it is set to 1440 minutes (24 hours). It is an absolute timeout. If the LTPA token times out, then user will be required to authenticate again. 

The following errors indicate that a user logged into TIP and did not log out and left the session open. After LTPA was timed-out, the user tried to access TIP again. This would generate the below error message in the log file. These errors can be ignored.

[3/29/12 14:54:01:535 CDT] 000000e5 LTPAServerObj W SECJ0371W: Validation of the LTPA token failed because the token expired with the following info: Token expiration Date: Thu Mar 29 14:53:00 CDT 2012, current Date: Thu Mar 29 14:54:01 CDT 2012.
[3/29/12 14:54:01:534 CDT] 000000e2 servlet E com.ibm.ws.webcontainer.servlet.ServletWrapper service SRVE0068E: Uncaught exception created in one of the service methods of the servlet /logon.jsp in application isc. Exception created : java.lang.IllegalStateException


See below technotes on how to change time out.
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21698519 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21698519]

1. Identify host/port of a client
    
    To identify a client which sent an expired LTPAToken, security auditing function can be used.
    
    Please refer to the instructions for security auditing [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/wasinfo/v7r0/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.websphere.nd.multiplatform.doc%2Finfo%2Fae%2Fae%2Ftsec_sa_secauditing.html]:
    To log the event, event name "SECURITY_AUTHN" and event outcome "DENIED" needs to be chosen. In this sample, DefaultAuditSpecification_2, which enable event "SECURITY_AUTHN and event outcome is DENIED, is used.
    
    Here is the sample output in SystemOut.log file:
    [4/19/12 10:45:30:244 EDT] 00000023 LTPAServerObj W SECJ0371W: Validation of the LTPA token failed because the token expired with the following info: Token expiration Date: Thu Apr 19 10:42:00 EDT 2012, current Date: Thu Apr 19 10:45:30 EDT 2012.

Most SECJ0371W messages on WEB Inbound connections are harmless. The majority of these messages are logged as a result of an expired LTPAToken which are cached in browsers. 

The following procedures will show you how to identify a client which sent an expired LTPAToken by way of a Web Inbound connection.

To address this issue, apply APAR JR39491 [http://www-933.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=ibm%2FWebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/WebSphere+Process+Server&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=7.0.0.3-WS-WBI-IFJR39491.zip&includeSupersedes=0&source=fc] as interim fix on WebSphere Process Server V7.
